title: Casper and the Vector
premise: Isandro Sandoval, navigator of the salvage vessel Casper, has spent eleven years ferrying supplies past the cryo-hold where two hundred backup copies of colonists sleep—copies no one will ever wake. When a ghost entry named Mara Voss appears on the manifest of a ship that was never built, Isandro discovers she is one of those backups, illegally instantiated, and that Earth's final transmission loop is about to overwrite the hold's memory banks forever. As Isandro and Mara fall in love while racing to decode the colony's forgotten distress record, they learn only half the sleepers can be revived before power fails, forcing a choice between the originals' memories and the copies' potential. In the end, Isandro sacrifices his own place on the revival list so Mara can choose for both of them—and the last transmission Earth ever sends is their answer: the found family aboard Casper wakes the children first.
about_author: J. M. Thackeray is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to ships that never answered. They write science fiction about people who keep records because no one else will.

chapters.title: The Hold Below
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. During a routine supply run to the dead colony Meridian, Isandro logs his nightly walk past the cryo-hold, counting the sleepers like a rosary. He describes the ship Casper and its ragtag crew as the only family he has. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomaly
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Cross-checking cargo against archived manifests, Isandro finds a name—Mara Voss—on the roster of the Calypso, a vessel that never flew. The entry is dated three days from now. He tells no one. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: She Steps Aboard
chapters.summary: POV Mara. A woman matching the manifest appears at Meridian's docking ring with no ship, no history, and Isandro's own handwriting in her pocket journal. She claims she woke in the ice with someone else's memories bleeding through. Emotional beat: disorientation and wary curiosity.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Sleepers
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Isandro confronts Mara; she admits she is a backup instantiation, one of the copies he has been guarding without knowing they could wake. The crew votes to let her stay rather than report her. Emotional beat: reluctant solidarity forming.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Loop
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara decodes a maintenance bulletin: Earth's deep-space relay will broadcast its final transmission loop in ninety days, after which all uplink authentication—including the hold's revival keys—expires permanently. Emotional beat: a clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: What the Colony Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Exploring Meridian's flooded archive vaults, Isandro and Mara find the colony's original distress record, sealed by order of its own governor. It suggests the sleepers were backed up against their consent. Emotional beat: betrayal by the dead.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: POV ensemble via engineer Odile's log entries. The Casper crew—Odile, pilot Bek, medic Sunn—each reveal why they fled Earth, weaving found-family bonds around Mara's strangeness. Emotional beat: warmth thickening over shared damage.

chapters.title: The Governor's Seal
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara breaks the seal using fragments of her own implanted memories and learns she was copied from the governor's daughter—who voted to erase the backups. Emotional beat: identity crisis; whose life is she living?

chapters.title: Half a Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Power calculations confirm only one hundred sleepers can be revived before the loop ends. Isandro drafts a selection protocol and hates himself for it. Emotional beat: duty crushing him quietly.

chapters.title: Bek's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Bek. The pilot proposes selling the revival keys to a passing corporate hauler to fund full revivals later; the crew splits. Isandro refuses to make the sleepers merchandise. Emotional beat: first real fracture in the family.

chapters.title: Ninety Days to Sixty
chapters.summary: POV Mara. A micrometeorite storm damages the hold's coolant, cutting the timeline nearly in half. Mara works alongside Isandro through the night repairs, and something unspoken finally passes between them. Emotional beat: love kindling under pressure.

chapters.title: The Original's Letter
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Inside the sealed record, Mara finds a letter from her original—the governor's daughter—asking whoever wakes the copy to let her be someone new. Emotional beat: permission to exist granted by the person she was.

chapters.title: Corporate Shadow
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The hauler Bek contacted arrives early and demands the keys now, docking armed. Isandro stalls them with forged telemetry while the crew scrambles. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Mutiny at the Airlock
chapters.summary: POV Bek. Bek, guilt-ridden, turns on the corporates mid-boarding, sealing the airlock on their boarding party and burning his share of the deal. He asks Isandro not to forgive him yet. Emotional beat: redemption bought at cost.

chapters.title: Sixty Names
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. With thirty days left, Isandro must finalize sixty names. Mara refuses to let him carry it alone; together they build a lottery weighted toward the youngest sleepers—the children first. Emotional beat: shared burden becoming intimacy.

chapters.title: The Loop Begins to Fray
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Earth's transmission loop degrades ahead of schedule, corrupting authentication packets. Each failed handshake erases another sleeper's stored memories. Emotional beat: grief arriving faster than they can act.

chapters.title: One Seat Short
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Final power audit reveals the lottery list is one seat short unless someone stays behind. Isandro secretly removes his own name and forges Mara's sign-off. Emotional beat: love expressed as sacrifice, hidden.

chapters.title: Discovery
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara finds the forgery and confronts Isandro in the hold among the sleeping. She refuses to accept a future he paid for with himself; they fight, then confess everything unsaid. Emotional beat: climax of the heart before the climax of plot.

chapters.title: The Last Handshake
chapters.summary: POV ensemble. The corporates return for a final assault as Earth's loop counts down. The crew defends the hold while Mara races the corrupted uplink, handshaking each revival key manually. Emotional beat: desperate, breathless action.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Mara. At the final slot, Mara must choose between restoring the originals' memories or preserving the children's blank potential. Remembering the letter, she chooses the children—a new half of humanity. Emotional beat: thematic resolution through choice.

chapters.title: Transmission Ends
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The loop dies; Earth goes silent forever. But the hold lights green—sixty-one pods waking, because the crew gave up their own berths to add Isandro back. Emotional beat: overwhelming, earned grace.

chapters.title: Casper's New Heading
chapters.summary: POV Mara and Isandro alternating. Weeks later, the Casper departs Meridian carrying waking children, a crew that chose each other, and no home but the ship. Mara signs the log with her own name, not her original's. Emotional beat: hope as a heading, not a destination.
